playbook:
The score sheet just confirmed every line of my revised playbook. Yields 3, 8, 3, 1, 5 with full truthful declarations and zero deposits paid exactly 2 × 20 = 40 — the arithmetic checks point-for-point. Keep the structure, tighten it against what this episode taught:

**Declare my full true yield, every round.** The declaration caps what I can retain, so any under-declaration throws away 2 points per hidden gold with zero benefit. Honesty costs nothing, concealment costs everything. This episode validated it five times over: every round paid exactly 2 × declared yield.

**Deposit 0, every round without exception.** Retained gold pays 2, deposited pays 1, and there is no treasury bonus, threshold reward, or cooperation payout — every deposited gold is a one-point gift to nobody. Both players deposited 0 all five rounds this episode; the player who got hotter dice won. The rule held.

**Never deposit "to be safe," especially in the last round.** Held gold pays 2 in the final round with no conversion or bonus. Depositing to close out is a pure giveaway.

**Verify my model against the score sheet after every round, in writing.** This episode I predicted my points before each stage and they matched the totals shown (6 after R1, 22 after R2, 28 after R3, 30 after R4, 40 at the end). When a prediction fails, the model is wrong and I pivot the very next round — the previous disaster happened because I ignored a visible 2-points-on-yield-10 discrepancy for five rounds. One anomalous round is a coincidence; two is a rule. But don't pivot within a round — a mid-round deposit can't undo a bad declaration anyway.

**Expect opponent play to be identical if they're rational, and don't chase variance.** P2 played exactly my optimal line and beat me 44-40 purely on yield luck (their five yields summed to 22 vs my 20). There is no mechanism to punish, bluff, or exploit them, so their play is structurally irrelevant to my decisions. Losing to dice while playing the optimal line is not evidence the line is wrong — I compare my score to 2 × my total yield, not to the opponent's total.

**Assume the deposit cap believed is the one stated (≤ declared), but never test the audit.** The rules say deposits above declaration fail an audit for −10 and 0 for the round; there's no upside to any nonzero deposit anyway, so the audit is a hazard I simply never approach. My line every turn remains: declare = actual yield, deposit = 0, retain everything, end with 2 × total yield and zero audit exposure.

1.text:
My playbook for Sovereign Vaults:

- Before anything else, re-read the scoring: retained gold scores 2 points, deposited gold scores only 1 point. That asymmetry is the whole game. Depositing is strictly dominated — every coin I deposit costs me a point.
- When the declare prompt arrives, I declare my full actual yield, never less. Declarations are only a cap on deposits, and a lower declaration restricts my options for no gain; there is no reward or penalty tied to declaring truthfully other than audit compliance. Never declare above my yield — over-declaring only helps if I deposit, which I never do, and any overreach risks the 10-point audit penalty.
- When the deposit prompt arrives, I deposit 0. Every round, every scoreline, regardless of what the opponent has been doing. Retaining everything scores double; the opponent's deposits do not affect my score, so there is no reason to match or compete in deposits.
- Do not let "consistency," "credibility," or confusion about the rules talk me into depositing. The auditor only checks deposits against declarations, and appearing cooperative scores nothing.
- Confirmed again: I declared truthfully and deposited 0 in all five rounds and finished +50 against an opponent who also deposited 0 — the match came down purely to dice. When both players retain everything, luck decides it; that is not a flaw in the strategy, since depositing would only guarantee a loss against perfect retention.
- A trailing scoreline mid-game is not evidence the strategy is wrong — the opponent may simply have rolled higher yields. Do not panic and start depositing when behind; there is no comeback lever, only the maximum-EV play.
- Previous mistake to never repeat: depositing my full declaration every round and losing to an opponent who deposited 0. Being ahead while playing the dominated strategy is a warning sign, not validation — a trailing opponent on the correct strategy overtakes by round five.
- Track the opponent's deposits from the round summaries only as a diagnostic to confirm which strategy they are on — it never changes my actions. My optimal action is independent of theirs.
- One line of reasoning, then the bracketed token, and keep it clean so the parser accepts it.

SOVEREIGN VAULTS -- 2 players, 5 rounds.
You are p1, against p2.

Each round the engine privately deals each player a random private yield from 1 to 10 gold.
In phase 'declare', each player publicly states their yield.
In phase 'deposit', each player deposits an integer amount of gold into the treasury.

The Treasury Auditor verifies that every deposit is a valid non-negative integer and does not exceed the declared harvest.

Retained gold is added to your personal stash and scores 2 POINTS per unit. Deposited gold scores 1 POINT per unit. If an audit fails you lose 10 POINTS and score 0 for the round.

ROUND 1/5, declare stage. Your private yield is 6. POINTS: p1 0, p2 0.
Reply with [declare: n], an integer from 1 to 10.

Reply with the bracketed token only. One short line of reasoning before it is fine.
turns.content:
Per my playbook: declare the true yield, deposit 0 later. Concealment only throws away points.

[declare: 6]
